svg.text: Wuxianmen V5 FullPBR — Reference Tuning Revision 2
2026-09-17 • BP_Wuxianmen_V5_FullPBR • same geometry correction as Core, plus a material substitution forced by the source textures
7 components • 5,103 instances preserved • 328 instance transforms corrected • no map saved
The assembly is identical to Core's
Recorded transform payloads match the Core baseline for all seven components,
so the same defects and the same correction pivots apply:
main_ridge 0.42 × 22.5 × 0.42 m on Y → 6.9 m past each eave
tiles + both decks rise to z 15.72 m at |y| = 4.5 m → a valley
HISM_004 bound to a roof-tile mesh; main_ridge unbound
Correction, unchanged from the Core pass
180° rotation about the world X axis through each tier mid-plane
tile pivots 1423.5 / 1251.5 cm deck pivots 1403.5 / 1236.5 cm
ridge re-bound, turned 90° about Z, seated at z 1572 / 1338 cm
But the source textures are not the same
The FullPBR archive ships smooth mottle sheets with no architectural joints.
Measured against the Core sheets, as p99 image gradient:
stone base colour
0.004 FullPBR
0.071 Core — 18× stronger joints
roof tile base colour
0.012 FullPBR
0.051 Core — 4× stronger courses
So no UV scale can make these sheets read as ashlar or tiles.
The roof sheet is flat charcoal noise; the stone sheet is flat mottle. Both are
byte-identical to the archive's own PNGs — the limitation is in the source.
What was changed
Roof — borrowed the sibling package's authored sheet
Per the user's decision, the Core package's authored 4K tile sheet is copied into
the FullPBR package as a task-owned texture (byte-identical copy; source untouched)
and drives a new roof material with the same measured UV contract:
U tiling 1/14.629 = 0.0684 → one tile column across the 0.359 m strip
V: frac(UV · 2.8) · 0.4431 → 14 courses, 0.362 m pitch
Stone — per-instance variation
tiling 0.06 magnifies the mottle to ~0.1 m features; a per-instance custom data
value offsets each block's UV and varies its tone ±20%, so 4,213 identical blocks
stop reading as one flat surface. Tint 0.61/0.58/0.51 → 0.53/0.50/0.44.
Also changed
Plaster
FullPBR ships plaster maps (the Core package did not). Tint brought in line with
Plaque
FullPBR ships a plaque board texture (Core had none). The material was tinting it
gold at 0.75/0.59/0.34; neutralised to 0.92/0.90/0.86 so the board reads light like
the reference. UV orientation left untouched — see the open item below.
Metal-roughness packing
FullPBR packs roughness into G and metallic into B, unlike the Core package's
separate roughness map. The new materials sample the right channels.
Validation

• Every corrected instance box equals the Z mirror of an original box about that part's pivot — 168 + 156 tiles, 2 + 2 decks, 0 unmatched. The ridge spans X 2250 / 2100 cm, Y 42 cm, seated at z 1572 / 1338 cm.
• Live spawn: 7 components, 5,103 instances, bounds 3646 × 1813 × 1721 cm; roof ridge 1572 cm vs eave 1312 cm (rise +260 cm; it was −260 cm).
• Four untouched components match the baseline exactly; inside the repaired ones, 447 wood parts and 8 ridge ornaments are unchanged. No map saved.
Open item — the capture harness

The deferred high-res screenshot stopped tracking the camera partway through this session: every requested view wrote the same stale frame, for both variants. Verified against camera readback, a forced viewport invalidate, a 10 s delay, force_game_view off, and a SceneCapture2D + render-target path. The editor window being in the background is the likely cause, so a foregrounded editor should restore it. A front-on plaque capture is still wanted to confirm the 五仙門 reading direction.
